original_question: Fix k >= 2. Does there exist m_0 such that whenever m >= m_0 and G is F_{2k+2}-free, then for each residue class l with 1 <= l <= k - 1 and m + k(k+1)/2 == l mod k, the graph G satisfies lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality only for that extremal graph?
target_in_paper: Section 3 of the survey, in the discussion of fan graphs F_t = K_1 ∨ P_{t-1}: specifically the nonzero-modulo fan-graph conjectures stated after Theorem 3.38, i.e. the even-fan/F_{2k+2}-free specialization of Conjectures 3.39–3.41, with later context from Theorem 3.48.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the main shape of the problem: k is fixed with k >= 2; one asks for an eventual-for-large-m extremal statement; the forbidden graph is F_{2k+2}; the problem is split by the residue class of m + k(k+1)/2 modulo k; the comparison is with a specific residue-class extremal construction S^{1,l}_{... ,k}; and the intended conclusion is a sharp spectral-radius inequality with uniqueness of the extremal graph.
missing_details: The paper works with simple finite undirected graphs; this should be stated explicitly.
In the survey’s standard notation one usually works in G(m,F), i.e. F-free graphs with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices; your draft does not state the no-isolated-vertices convention.
F_{2k+2} should be defined explicitly as the fan graph K_1 ∨ P_{2k+1}.
lambda(G) should be defined explicitly as the adjacency spectral radius, i.e. the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix A(G) over the reals.
The graph family S^{1,l}_{... ,k} is not defined in the draft; without the paper’s definition, the question is not stand-alone.
The quantifier on m_0 should be made precise: it should depend on k (and in the paper-faithful formulation, not on G or m).
The phrase 'for each residue class l' should be rewritten so that l is quantified first and the congruence condition is attached cleanly.
The congruence should be written with ≡ mod k rather than '=='.
It should be made explicit that equality means equality up to graph isomorphism, i.e. G ≅ S^{1,l}_{... ,k}.
The draft does not explain why the parameter (m-l)/k + (k+3)/2 is an integer; this integrality is hidden in the residue-class condition.

If one wants the formulation to be fully paper-faithful, it should be clear that this is the nonzero residue-class version of the fan-graph problem, following the already resolved 0-mod-k case in Theorem 3.38.
refined_question: Fix an integer k >= 2, let F_{2k+2} = K_1 ∨ P_{2k+1}, and write lambda(G) for the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of a simple graph G. In the notation of the paper, is it true that there exists m_0 = m_0(k) such that, for every integer m >= m_0, every l in {1, ..., k-1} with m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ l (mod k), and every F_{2k+2}-free graph G with m edges and no isolated vertices, one has lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality if and only if G is isomorphic to S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}?
justification: The fan-graph family in your draft matches the survey’s Section 3 discussion of F_t = K_1 ∨ P_{t-1}. The survey first records the solved congruence-0 case for fan graphs in Theorem 3.38, then states further modulo-class conjectures (Conjectures 3.39–3.41) for the remaining residue classes, and finally notes that a later general theorem (Theorem 3.48) subsumes at least part of this program. Because your draft keeps the fan-graph hypothesis F_{2k+2}-free and asks for the nonzero residue classes with a residue-dependent extremal graph S^{1,l}_{... ,k}, the nearest paper-faithful target is the even-fan specialization of those post-Theorem-3.38 modulo-case conjectures, not the earlier basic join-graph statement alone. The main incompleteness in the draft is that it leaves the paper’s extremal construction S^{1,l}_{... ,k} undefined and omits the survey’s ambient conventions (simple graphs, adjacency spectral radius, and the no-isolated-vertices G(m,F) setting).
